question.text: Which place will Japan receive the most foreign visitors from during November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the country or area with the highest number of visitor arrivals to Japan during November 2026, according to the [Japan National Tourism Organization](https://statistics.jnto.go.jp/en/graph/#graph--latest--figures).
question.fine_print: Non-country entities counted separately by the JNTO will count separately for the purpose of this question.

research:
South Korea has been Japan's largest source of visitors in every 2026 month I could check, and by a wide margin. China has been far behind since Beijing told its citizens to avoid Japan in November 2025.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-10: The JNTO graph page doesn't show figures in text form; they are in PDFs that require a data usage application form. I couldn't parse the JNTO PDFs directly, so the figures below come from JNTO press pages and Japanese trade press citing JNTO. [JNTO stats](https://statistics.jnto.go.jp/en/graph/)
- 2026-10-21: The latest release is September 2026, with 3,103,700 arrivals in total (down 5.0% year on year). [JNTO press](https://www.jnto.go.jp/news/press/20261021_monthly.html)
  - South Korea: 842,300 (up 25.6%)
  - Taiwan: 595,600 (up 13%)
  - China: 430,800 (down 44.5%)
  - Hong Kong and the US were both down (3.0% and 3.2%). [Travel Voice](https://www.travelvoice.jp/20261021-160712)
- JNTO lists Korea and Taiwan among the 7 markets with a record September. [JNTO press](https://www.jnto.go.jp/news/press/20261021_monthly.html)

## 2. Current status
- The question isn't settled; November data comes out around mid-December. All recent monthly data points to South Korea, with Taiwan second and China third.
- 2026-09-16: In August, South Korea had 850,500 (up 28.7%, the largest of the 23 key markets) and Taiwan 666,000. China had 418,000 (down 59%, its 9th straight monthly decline), Hong Kong 247,300 and the US 197,400. [Travel Voice](https://www.travelvoice.jp/20260916-160529), [nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/ja/japan-data/h02895/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-08: According to OAG, Seoul Incheon to Tokyo Narita is the world's busiest international route in November 2026, with 549,928 seats (up 42% year on year). Incheon to Osaka Kansai is third with 473,424 seats (up 16%). [VnExpress](https://e.vnexpress.net/news/travel/9-of-10-busiest-international-flight-routes-in-november-are-in-asia-pacific-5140781.html)
- 2026-11-08: Japan's new tax-free shopping system took effect on November 1. Tourists now pay the tax at the till and claim a refund when they leave. [Tourism Review](https://www.tourism-review.com/new-rules-for-tax-free-shopping-introduced-in-japan-news15708)
- 2026-10-21: JNTO blamed China's decline on Beijing's travel warning and fewer flights. Across all markets, it also pointed to higher airfares linked to the Middle East situation and typhoon cancellations. [Travel Voice](https://www.travelvoice.jp/20261021-160712)
- 2026-01-26: China renewed its advisory telling citizens to avoid travel to Japan "in the near term". About 50 China-Japan routes were suspended in February. I couldn't confirm the advisory's status as of November 2026, and I found no sign that it has been lifted. [VisaHQ](https://www.visahq.com/news/2026-01-27/cn/china-cautions-citizens-against-japan-travel-over-spring-festival-major-airlines-waive-change-fees/)

## 4. Base rates
- November 2025 (when the advisory was announced mid-month): South Korea 824,500, China 562,600, Taiwan 542,400 and Hong Kong 207,600. Total arrivals were 3.518 million. [nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/ja/japan-data/h02644/), [JNTO](https://www.jnto.go.jp/news/press/20251217_monthly.html)
- South Korea also topped November 2024 and most months of 2023 and 2024, apart from China's peak months in 2025.
- In August and September 2026, Korea led Taiwan by about 185,000 and 247,000, and led China by about 410,000 to 430,000. Applying recent growth rates to the November 2025 figures, with Korea up about 25%, Taiwan up about 10% and China down about 45 to 60%, gives roughly 1.0 million for Korea, 600,000 for Taiwan and 250,000 to 310,000 for China. This is a rough extrapolation.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the collected market prices match this question; they cover Hawaii arrivals, Japan GDP, the Bank of Japan and others.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or expert forecast on Japan's top source market for November 2026.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around 2026-11-18: JNTO is expected to publish its October 2026 estimate. The date is inferred from its usual mid-month schedule.
- Around 2026-12-16: The November 2026 estimate, which settles this question, is expected.
- Possible disruptions: a sudden thaw between China and Japan with flights restored (none seen so far), a shock to Japan-Korea travel, or a major typhoon or airline disruption. Even an immediate thaw would struggle to close a gap of more than 400,000 within one month.

- South Korea also topped November in 2023 and 2024. China was the top source in many months of 2025 before the dispute. I didn't re-verify every month.
- Rough guide for November 2026: if the September growth rates held (Korea +25%, Taiwan +13%, China -45%), Korea would be about 1.0 million, Taiwan about 610,000 and China about 310,000. That is a straight extrapolation from the numbers above, not a forecast.
- Taiwan has been about 250,000 behind Korea, and Hong Kong is far behind at about 145,000. I couldn't confirm month-by-month figures for January to June 2026.

One commercial source (Chinese Tourists Agency) sees Chinese arrivals moving from decline to flat or a slight recovery, with no full recovery in the near term. forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** November 2026 arrivals will be known when JNTO publishes its estimate, around 16 December 2026. That is about 5 weeks away, and the month itself has only just started.

(b) **Status quo:** South Korea is first. It has led every 2026 month checked, with Taiwan a distant second and China third.

(c) **Base rates:** South Korea was top in November 2024 and November 2025, and in most months of 2023 to 2026. China was top only in its peak months of 2025, before the travel advisory. Taiwan and Hong Kong have not been top in any recent month. Other markets, such as the US, have never come close.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **September 2026 (released 21 October):**
  - South Korea: 842,300, up 25.6%
  - Taiwan: 595,600
  - China: 430,800, down 44.5%
- **August 2026 (released 16 September):**
  - South Korea: 850,500
  - Taiwan: 666,000
  - China: 418,000
- **November 2025:** South Korea was first with 824,500, even before China's decline had fully taken hold.
- **OAG data for November 2026 (reported 8 November):** Incheon to Narita is the world's busiest international route, with seats up 42% year on year. Incheon to Kansai is third, up 16%. This points to strong Korean capacity this month.
- **China:** I found no sign that the travel advisory has been lifted, and flights remain reduced.

(e) **Unexpected outcome scenario:** A severe shock to Korea-Japan travel would be needed. Examples are a major airline crisis or safety event on Korean carriers, a sudden diplomatic rupture, or a natural disaster that hits Korean demand in particular. Combined with an unusually strong Taiwanese month, this could cut a lead of roughly 250,000 to 400,000. A sudden China thaw could not rebuild a gap of more than 400,000 within November. Data revisions or reclassification are another remote path.

**Reasoning:** I start from the base rate, which already strongly favours Korea, at about 90%. I moved up to about 95% for three reasons:
- The current gaps are very large.
- November seat capacity points to further Korean strength.
- China's recovery path remains blocked.

I keep a few percent on Taiwan as the realistic runner-up, and small tails on the other options.

Option_A: 0.015
Option_B: 0.95
Option_C: 0.03
Option_D: 0.0025
Option_E: 0.0025
